### Purging Iniquity
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/purging-iniquity
Passage: Zechariah 5:3
Points:
- The flying scroll reflects the covenant curses of the Mosaic law directed against impenitent sinners.
- The consumption of the offenders' houses illustrates God's judgment consuming sin itself rather than utterly destroying His redeemed community.
- Combined with the companion basket vision, the text portrays the expiation and total removal of wickedness from the camp.
- The vision points forward to Jesus Christ, who took upon Himself the full curse of the law.
- Through Christ's death and resurrection, sin is buried and stripped of its condemning power.

### Our Sins Are Many, His Mercy Is More
Author: Ryan Shelton
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/our-sins-are-many-his-mercy-is-more
Passage: Zechariah 5:4
Points:
- Christians frequently oscillate between treating sin as trivial and despairing that it is too large for God to cleanse.
- The flying scroll entering evildoers' homes demonstrates that sins like theft and lying pollute God's dwelling place.
- Corporate worship serves as a weekly unrolling of the scroll, exposing the gravity of our hidden offenses.
- While the vision reveals the weight of judgment, God effortlessly removes and banishes our wickedness.
- Jesus Christ bore the consuming curse on the cross, purifying His people to be His new temple.
